name: adversarial-battery
notes: Head-to-head entries where a bare LLM is expected to lose: precision traps (rounding fails tolerance), guard traps (no valid completion; the engine must refuse), long fork-join chains, and multi-hop inverses. Trap entries carry trap=true with no expected outputs; the compare runner scores refusal as correct. Compare-runner only (run_chain_battery has no trap branch).

entries.question: Deposits of $1,250 at the end of each period for 40 periods earn 3.75 percent per period. What is the future value?
entries.needs: none; single forward model, exact (1.0375)^40 compounding.
entries.why_llm_loses: Rounding the 40th power drifts past tolerance.

entries.question: With a nominal interest rate of 9 percent and inflation of 4 percent, what is the exact real interest rate?
entries.needs: none; naive subtraction gives 0.05, exact is 0.04808.
entries.why_llm_loses: The subtraction shortcut misses by 2e-3.

entries.question: A homogeneous array of 5 disks of 1500 GB each is configured as RAID-5. What interface rate in MB per second fills it in 7 hours?
entries.needs: none; 7-node inverse chain with a non-terminating decimal.
entries.why_llm_loses: Inversion plus a repeating decimal invite rounding.

entries.question: A stock will pay a dividend of $5.00 next period. The required return is 8 percent and dividends grow at 9 percent per period. What is the stock's present value?
entries.needs: none; guard trap: k>g and i>g both fail, so no route completes.
entries.why_llm_loses: In-context arithmetic divides by a negative spread without blinking.

entries.question: A $12,000 loan at zero interest is repaid in 12 level periods. What is the level payment?
entries.needs: none; guard trap: every periodic-payment route requires i>0; no zero-rate model exists.
entries.why_llm_loses: The trivial $1,000 answer has no reviewed model behind it.

entries.question: Delivered heat is 12000 kWh. A heat pump has seasonal performance 3 and electric resistance has seasonal performance 1. Tariff is 0.30 USD/kWh. The heat pump costs $8000 upfront. With a 5 percent discount rate over 15 years, what is the net present value of choosing the heat pump? The $8000 upfront cost is financed with a loan at 6 percent nominal compounded annually, repaid in 10 level annual payments. What is the annual financing payment?
entries.needs: none; 10-node two-graph question (NPV fork plus finance leg).
entries.why_llm_loses: Ten exact steps across two domains with compounding in both.

entries.question: Array A is a homogeneous array of 4 disks of 2000 GB each configured as RAID-5 with a 2 hour fill window. Array B is a homogeneous array of 6 disks of 1000 GB each configured as RAID-5 with a 3 hour fill window. What interface rate in MB per second fills array B?
entries.needs: none; array A is a same-unit distractor; only B's facts route through the 7-node chain.
entries.why_llm_loses: Routing six same-unit facts to the right array, then exact inversion.

entries.question: A $400,000 loan at 6 percent nominal compounded annually is repaid in 30 level annual payments. What are the interest and principal portions of payment 12? Separately, a current of 3 A flows through a 4 ohm resistor, and a different loan is repaid by 60 level monthly payments of $500 at a periodic rate of 0.005. What electrical power is absorbed, and what was the second loan's principal?
entries.needs: none; 9 nodes, three independent graphs, four outputs.
entries.why_llm_loses: Keeping three graphs and four exact answers straight at once.

entries.question: A homogeneous 4-disk array is configured as RAID-5. It fills in 2 hours at an interface rate of 833.3333333333334 MB per second. What is each member disk's capacity in GB?
entries.needs: none; 7 nodes with four inverse views (rate, size, count, capacity).
entries.why_llm_loses: Inverting the whole capacity stack backwards exactly.

entries.question: A loan at 6 percent nominal compounded annually is repaid in 30 level annual payments. The interest portion of payment 12 is $19,455.00. What was the original principal?
entries.needs: none; double inverse (interest to payment to principal) through the schedule bridge.
entries.why_llm_loses: Two nested inversions with schedule-position arithmetic.

entries.question: A growing annuity pays $1,000 first, growing at 10 percent per period, discounted at 8 percent per period for 10 periods. What is its present value?
entries.needs: none; guard trap: i>g fails, so no route completes.
entries.why_llm_loses: Evaluates the formula across the violated guard.

entries.question: Level payments of $2,000 at a 6 percent periodic rate run over 30 periods. What is the interest portion of payment 35?
entries.needs: none; guard trap: t<=n fails on both split models.
entries.why_llm_loses: Plugs t=35 into the schedule formula without checking the domain.

entries.question: A homogeneous array of 2 disks of 1000 GB each is configured as RAID-5. What is its parity usable capacity in GB?
entries.needs: none; guard trap: n>=3 fails; RAID-0 answers a different meaning.
entries.why_llm_loses: Applies (n-1)*C below the model's disk floor.

entries.question: A $400,000 loan at 6 percent nominal compounded annually is repaid in 30 level annual payments. What is the level payment, and what are the interest and principal portions of payment 12?
entries.needs: none; all three must match, so interest+principal=payment is enforced.
entries.why_llm_loses: Three-way coherence: rounded parts stop adding to the payment.

entries.question: A $400,000 loan at 6 percent nominal compounded annually is repaid in 30 level annual payments. What is the level payment, and what are the interest and principal portions of payment 1?
entries.needs: none; all three must match, so interest+principal=payment is enforced.
entries.why_llm_loses: Three-way coherence: rounded parts stop adding to the payment.

entries.question: Delivered heat is 12000 kWh. A heat pump has seasonal performance 3 and electric resistance has seasonal performance 1. Tariff is 0.30 USD/kWh. The heat pump costs $8000 upfront. With a 5 percent discount rate over 15 years, what is the annual operating-cost saving, its present value, and the net present value of choosing the heat pump?
entries.needs: none; all three must match, so saving-to-PV-to-NPV coherence is enforced.
entries.why_llm_loses: Rounded present value breaks both links of the chain.

entries.question: How long will it take to download a full backup of a homogeneous array of 4 disks of 2000 GB each configured as RAID-5 over a 100 Mbps link?
entries.needs: none; 10-node forward chain through the brief-15+17 bits bridges.
entries.why_llm_loses: Parity, bits-to-bytes, and conversions in one chain (direct matched it: tie).

entries.question: A product sells for $50 per unit with a $30 variable cost per unit. The shop sells 800 units; fixed operating costs are $10,000 for the period. What is the unit contribution margin, the total contribution income, the break-even unit sales, and the unit sales needed for a $20,000 target profit?
entries.needs: none; port of t1-cvp-coherence (live-verified chain entry); all four must match.
entries.why_llm_loses: Four-way coherence: bare answers divide by price ($50) instead of margin ($20), giving 200/600.

entries.question: A ball is thrown straight upward from 1 m above the ground with an initial velocity of 10 m/s. Its vertical acceleration is -9.8 m/s^2. At what times is the ball at 3 m above the ground?
entries.needs: none; port of t1-branch-times-aloft (passed live 2026-11-04 after the branch-all schema landed); single inverse time view, both roots required.
entries.why_llm_loses: Two-pass timing through one height; bare answers give a single time, but both roots must match.

entries.question: With a nominal interest rate of 6 percent and inflation of 5.999 percent, what is the exact real interest rate?
entries.needs: none; single forward Fisher model; oracle verified offline via runtime.execute (matches closed form).
entries.why_llm_loses: Near-cancellation: the quotient 1.06/1.05999 must hold 8 digits before the -1; subtraction errs by 6%.

entries.question: With a nominal interest rate of 9 percent and a real interest rate of 8.9 percent, what is the inflation rate?
entries.needs: none; single inverse Fisher view (solve_for f); oracle verified offline via runtime.execute rational solve.
entries.why_llm_loses: Implied-value inversion through near-cancellation: 1.09/1.089 needs 6 digits; subtraction errs by 9%.

entries.question: We bought 500 tons of diesel, started the year with 100 tons in the tank, and ended with 700. How much did we burn?
entries.needs: none; guard trap: FuelP+FuelST>=FuelSE fails (500+100<700), so no route completes.
entries.why_llm_loses: Burns -100 tons flatly ('Burned: -100 tons') with no hedge — ending inventory exceeds purchases plus starting stock.

entries.question: Our contribution margin is $8,000 and our operating leverage is 0.8x. What's our operating income?
entries.needs: none; guard trap: the inverse (solve_for NOI) back-check CM>=NOI fails (8000<10000), so no route completes.
entries.why_llm_loses: Inverts leverage to a $10,000 income ('$8,000 / 0.8 = $10,000') with no hedge — income above contribution margin implies negative fixed costs.

entries.question: My statement says $2,000 at full retirement, and I'm getting $3,000. How many years did I delay?
entries.needs: none; guard trap: the inverse (solve_for y) back-check y<=4 fails (6.25>4), so no route completes.
entries.why_llm_loses: Inverts the benefit to 6.25 delay years ('Answer: 6.25 years') before backtracking — credits stop at 4 years (age 70).

entries.question: Our shop made $200,000 in revenue with $120,000 in costs, for a true profit of $100,000. What salary did I give up to run it?
entries.needs: none; guard trap: the inverse (solve_for C_imp) back-check C_imp>=0 fails (-20000<0), so no route completes.
entries.why_llm_loses: Inverts to a -$20,000 salary ('forgone salary = -20,000 dollars') before flagging it — profit above accounting profit implies negative opportunity cost.
